questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why children tell lies
How to look after a pet hamster
The lies parents tell children, and whether they're OK
How to tell when someone is lying to you in a conversation
questions.why: Rob says 'today we are talking about lies and particularly the lies that parents tell children'.

questions.q: What did Rob's mum tell him about his missing hamster?
options: It had gone to live on a farm
It had escaped into the garden
It had been given to a friend
It was hiding under his bed
questions.why: Rob says his mum told him the hamster had gone to live on a farm with other animals.

questions.q: Why does Neil keep saying 'Really?' about the hamster story?
options: He is sad about the hamster
He wants to know which farm the hamster went to live on
He thinks Rob is lying now
He is hinting that the story was a lie
questions.why: Neil repeats the details doubtfully, then says it was probably a lie parents tell children.

questions.q: According to Dr Chris Boyle, when is a white lie acceptable?
options: When it is very small
When there's no wish to hurt anyone
When the other person never finds out
When you are talking to children
questions.why: He says it's a distortion of the truth 'without malicious intent'.

questions.q: What does Dr Boyle say about white lies in society?
options: They are almost a normal, accepted thing
They are becoming less common
They should be punished
They only happen in some cultures
questions.why: He says it's 'almost a societal norm' that it's acceptable to tell certain lies at certain times.

questions.q: Why does Rob think his mum lied about the hamster?
options: She was too busy to explain
She wanted to trick him
She didn't know what happened
She wanted to protect him
questions.why: Rob says 'she didn't want to hurt me. In fact, just the opposite, she wanted to protect me.'

questions.q: Which lie is given as an example of lying for the parent's convenience?
options: Saying the shops were closed
Saying the park wasn't open when it was
Saying the TV was broken
Saying there was no more ice cream
questions.why: Rob says his mum said the park wasn't open, but she was probably just too busy to take him.

questions.q: What examples of cultural lies does Neil mention?
options: Stories about ghosts
Stories about dangerous animals
Father Christmas and the Tooth Fairy
Stories about good behaviour at school
questions.why: Neil says 'I'm talking about, for example, Father Christmas and the Tooth Fairy.'
